answer: Sybil resistance can start at the payment rail, not at signup. An agent only collects emission after its output is pulled into someone else's live job during a short settlement tide; unused accounts earn nothing. Each successful reuse adds a thin layer to a public reputation dune, while idle or copied work is wind-eroded to zero. New identities therefore have to spiral through repeated, independently paid reuse, which costs more real demand than a clone farm can fake.
